source_kind_detail: issuer-hosted XLSX (all SPDR US ETFs historical distributions, single sheet 'dividend'), filtered to TICKER == BIL; the same workbook URL as SPY.csv
fetch_method: curl -L GET inside the default sandbox (no sandbox override), desktop Chrome User-Agent; Content-Type application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet; Date header Fri, 16 Oct 2026 09:03:08 GMT; Last-Modified Fri, 16 Oct 2026 04:18:30 GMT
cutoff_requested: none: every issuer record at capture (all ex-dates are on or before the capture date)
parsing_notes: Workbook has one sheet ('dividend'): a header row and 13384 rows below it, of which 53 carry no ticker (blank rows and trailing notice text) and the rest cover 181 SPDR US ETF tickers; every cell is a shared string (dates MM/DD/YYYY, amounts as decimal strings with six decimals). Selected the 232 rows with TICKER == 'BIL' (single CUSIP 78468R663, FREQUENCY 'Monthly' on every row). amount = DIVIDEND ($) + SHORT TERM CAPITAL GAIN ($) + LONG TERM CAPITAL GAIN ($) per share, summed as decimals (blank treated as 0). Two rows carry a cash capital-gain component: ex 2008-12-29 = dividend 0.017152 + STCG 0.011056 = 0.028208, and ex 2009-12-29 = STCG 0.003815 alone. 105 rows have a zero amount: every BIL ex-date from 2009-12-01 through 2016-11-01 except 2009-12-29 (0.003815) and 2011-12-28 (0.001893), and every one from 2020-06-01 through 2022-05-02 except 2020-12-01 (0.003251), the near-zero rate periods; the issuer lists them as distributions of 0.000000 and they are kept as zero cash events, not dropped. No duplicate ex-dates, so nothing was summed across rows. Parsed with zipfile + xml.etree, as for SPY.csv; the same parser applied to this capture reproduces the tracked SPY.csv's 135 rows byte for byte (the capture holds one later SPY row, ex 2026-09-18), which checks the parser, not the BIL amounts. Cadence: 12 ex-dates in every full calendar year 2008-2025, 7 in 2007 (first ex-date 2007-07-02) and 9 in 2026 through 2026-10-01; gaps over 45 days (46 days, mid-December to early February 2022, 2025, 2026) are the issuer's second December ex-date with no January one. RECORD DATE is in the raw file but not carried into the CSV.
anomalies: ex 2008-03-03 carries PAYABLE DATE 02/11/2008, before its ex-date (and equal to the previous row's pay date). It is written as the issuer lists it and not corrected; a consumer that credits cash on the pay date should not rely on this row's pay date.
cross_check: none independent: the workbook is the only source read for BIL (no product-page or non-issuer comparison was made)
